title: I hope this musical has another run… wait for it… Soon!  #theatrerevi...
transcript: I really enjoyed this. I've heard people rave about the East Village basement as a location, and I've never seen a show there. So it only makes sense that the first show I would see there would be an intimate chamber musical about the end of the world. And I would tell you to go see it, but unfortunately it's entire two week run is sold out. So keep, keep an eye on the SOON, because I. I do not think we've seen the last of this for sure. SOON is a very intimate musical that examines if you found out the world as you know it was ending, how would you cope? How would you deal with the fact that the days are numbered? Right. And I feel like that's something that is so incredibly relevant right now because if for many days it does feel like we are watching the world around us crumble. And in this intimate musical, we follow Charlie, who is essentially living in this apartment that we're all sitting in, and she decides to just not leave that apartment. That is, that is her coping mechanism and how the people around her react to that decision. There's so much I absolutely love about this show from the intimate staging. Like, I'm curious how it would work in a larger space, because I do think, especially with how well it's sold, they would wanna go to a larger space eventually. But part of it That was so beautiful was the intimacy. Some incredible staging by Will Blum, who I know as an actor and has stepped into the director chair for the show, and just really, really creative choices. You have some really gorgeous songs in this, written by Nick Blaemire, who also wrote and co wrote shows like Glory Days and Space Dogs and safety not guaranteed. Because it's in this intimate space, you only have three musicians playing a variety of different string instruments, and they just. Ah! The orchestration sounded gorgeous. And ultimately, while I think the writing just needs a little bit of polish, there was. There was parts of the emotional arc that didn't quite land the way that I think they want to land right now. Ultimately, this is a show that stuck the landing, and that. That I think is, you know, one of the biggest hurdles in creating a new musical is. Is your show sticking the landing? This one absolutely does. There were moments where I felt the songs went on just a little too long or they didn't quite start progressing the story. It felt like we were a little stagnant, which could be intentional, because a lot of this is about staying stagnant. But I think there's a way to do that that still keeps those songs moving forward. But there's something so special about getting to see this show in such an intimate space and with this incredible cast, especially mylinda Hull who Absolutely a scene stealer as Charley's mother. She was just hilarious every time she came on the stage. And such a fully fleshed out character. I am excited to see what happens with this musical next and how it continues to evolve. It's been a long time in development, but I'm sure we have not seen the last of it yet. Especially with the fact that this is sold out. I believe they do have a cancellation list. It is only a two week run until November 9th. So if you wanna try to get on the cancellation list, you absolutely can. But, uh, the. The run is completely sold out. And for good reason. I cannot wait to see what happens with it next.
